ns2:section.sectionText: TOPIC TITLE: "Ecology and Natural Disasters in Colonial Spanish America." This course will offer a historical perspective of the way ecology, natural disasters, and human actions are intrinsically intertwined. We will examine visual and written materials that depict and articulate how natural disasters and climate in general have impacted human interactions and ecosystems in Spanish America from the early modern period to contemporary times. Finally, we will particularly focus on the manner in which cultural identities are affected by the way ecosystems are changed and transformed. Students must meet the prerequisite requirements for this course (found in the Catalog Entry) or will be told to drop on the first day of classes. Non-registered students are not allowed to sit in or audit.
